mainTopic: When workers carrying pure food keep it pure, and the משנה's list of ways קודש is stricter than תרומה
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about workers who are עמי הארץ carrying an owner's pure food. If the owner simply walks far away, the food stays pure. If he tells them 'Go, I'll come after you' and loses sight of them, it becomes impure. The גמרא asks why, and רבי יצחק נפחא says that in the first case the workers had purified themselves. After a back-and-forth about other עמי הארץ touching the food, the גמרא concludes that in the first case the workers fear the owner may appear from any side, so they stay careful. In the second case they think he is behind them, so they relax. Then פרק אין דורשין ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה listing ways that קודש has stricter purity rules than תרומה. These rules cover dipping vessels, carrying a מדרס, knots, new vessels, levels of impurity, impure hands, and eating dry food.

steps.title: A ברייתא about workers carrying pure food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. If the owner simply walks far away, his pure food stays pure. If he tells the workers to go ahead and loses sight of them, it becomes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: If someone's donkey drivers and workers were carrying pure food, even if he went more than a מיל away from them, his pure food is pure. But if he told them, 'Go, and I will come after you,' once they are out of his sight, his pure food is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the words 'וְהָתַנְיָא' (but isn't it taught?). It uses the ברייתא to push against what was said just before about losing focus on pure items (היסח הדעת).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to say that distance alone does not make the food impure. Yet in the second case, simply losing sight of the workers does make it impure. This sets up a puzzle that the rest of the passage will try to solve.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure foods or items that are kept ritually pure
His eyes lost sight of them
A measure of distance, about 2,000 אמות

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
One whose donkey drivers and workers
phrases.notes: These workers are עמי הארץ, people who are not careful about purity.

phrases.english: were carrying pure foods,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִפְלִיג מֵהֶן יוֹתֵר מִמִּיל —
phrases.english: even though he went away from them more than a מיל —
his pure foods are pure.
But if he said to them:
'Go, and I will come after you,'
once his eyes lost sight of them —
his pure foods are impure.

steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier discussion of היסח הדעת (losing focus on pure items)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows the food can stay pure even when the owner is far away, so distance alone does not seem to cause impurity.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first case is pure and the second is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what separates the two halves of the ברייתא. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the owner is not watching the workers. So why does one stay pure and the other become impure? The גמרא wants a clear reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: What is different about the first case
and what is different about the last case?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what explains the two different rulings in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the first case is pure and the last case is impure

steps.title: The workers were purified beforehand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא explains that in the first case, the owner had his workers purify themselves for this job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: The first case is where he purified his donkey drivers and workers for this purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא answers the question. In the first case, the workers had already made themselves pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the workers themselves are pure, their touch does not make the food impure. So the owner's distance does not matter. This explains why the first case is pure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
The first case is where he purifies his donkey drivers and workers for this purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by limiting the first case to a specific situation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first case is where the workers had already purified themselves for carrying the food.

steps.title: Then the last case should also be pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if purified workers are enough, the last case should be pure too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the last case should also be pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק נפחא's answer. If the owner purifies the workers in the last case too, why would that food be impure?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purifying the workers should protect the food in both cases. So the answer does not seem to explain why the last case is different.

phrases.english: If so, the last case also!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: the last case should also be pure if the workers were purified.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If purifying the workers keeps the food pure, it should work in the last case as well.

steps.title: Other עמי הארץ might touch the food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that an עם הארץ does not mind if another עם הארץ touches him or the food. On the way, someone impure may have touched it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An עם הארץ is not careful about his friend's touch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last case. Even pure workers do not stop other עמי הארץ from touching the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry in the last case is no longer the workers themselves. It is other people they meet on the road. Once the owner is out of sight, the workers have no reason to keep others away.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone not careful about purity laws

phrases.english: An עם הארץ is not careful
about the touch of his friend.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a new source of impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only worry was the workers themselves, and purifying them solved it.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is also a worry that other עמי הארץ on the way will touch the food.

steps.title: Then the first case should also be impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the same worry about other עמי הארץ should apply in the first case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the first case should also be impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the new answer around. If others might touch the food, that could happen in the first case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the owner is also more than a מיל away. So other עמי הארץ could also reach the food there. Now the first case seems hard to explain.

phrases.english: If so, the first case also!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: the first case should also be impure because of other people's touch.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer about other עמי הארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about other עמי הארץ touching the food should apply equally in the first case.

steps.title: The owner might appear from a winding path
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the first case is where the owner reaches them by a winding route. The workers never know when he might show up, so they stay careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first case is where he comes to them by a winding path.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the first case: the owner could pop up at any moment from an unexpected direction. This is not the end yet, because the next step challenges this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the workers fear he might suddenly appear from the side, they stay careful the whole time. That includes keeping other עמי הארץ away from the food. This removes the worry raised in step 6 for the first case, but the גמרא will next ask why the same fear doesn't apply in the last case.

phrases.english: Where he comes to them
by a winding path.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: In the first case, the workers had no reason to keep other people away.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the first case, the workers fear the owner may appear suddenly, so they guard the food from everyone.

steps.title: The winding-route answer should also work for the last case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer. If the owner might suddenly show up by a winding route, that worry should also keep the workers careful in the last case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the last case should be pure too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 7. The worry that the owner could pop up at any moment seems just as real in the last case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the workers stay careful because they never know when the owner will appear. But in the last case the owner could also come by a winding route. So why should that case be impure?

phrases.english: If so, the last case too [should be pure]!
phrases.notes: The 'last case' is where the owner told the workers he would come after them, and the items were ruled impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the תירוץ of step 7 by applying it to the other case
steps.kashyaTarget: The winding-route explanation for the first case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner could arrive suddenly in the last case as well, so the workers there should also stay careful.

steps.title: Being told 'I will come after you' makes the workers relax
steps.stepSummary: In the last case the owner told the workers he would follow behind them. So they assume he is behind them and are not careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he told them, 'Go, and I will come after you,' they rely on that and feel relaxed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The owner's own words make the workers feel he won't surprise them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the workers have no idea where the owner is, so they stay alert. In the last case he told them he is coming behind them, so they don't expect him to pop up ahead. Because of that, they may let other עמי הארץ touch them, and the items are impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Go, and I will come after you
Their minds rely on it (they feel settled and relaxed)

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between the cases depends on what the workers expect. Not knowing where the owner is keeps them careful. Hearing he is behind them makes them relax.

phrases.english: Since he said to them
'Go, and I will come after you'
their minds rely on it.
phrases.notes: He means they feel safe, thinking the owner is behind them and won't catch them off guard.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the workers' state of mind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chance of a surprise visit should keep workers careful in both cases
steps.terutzMaskana: Once told the owner is coming behind them, the workers relax, so the last case stays impure

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אין דורשין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the second פרק of חגיגה, אין דורשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, אין דורשין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line simply marks the end of the פרק called אין דורשין. A new פרק begins right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is a traditional goodbye to a finished פרק, promising to come back and learn it again. It does not add any new law.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (closing formula for a פרק)
Name of the second פרק of חגיגה

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Ein Dorshin'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק אין דורשין is complete.

steps.title: New פרק: vessel rules where קודש is stricter than תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says קודש has stricter purity rules than תרומה. Its first examples are about dipping vessels in a מקוה and about treating parts of a vessel separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: קודש is treated more strictly than תרומה. You may dip vessels inside other vessels to purify them for תרומה, but not for קודש. The back, the inside, and the gripping place of a vessel are treated as separate parts for תרומה, but not for קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It starts a list of ways that holy sacrificial food (קודש) needs more purity care than תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תרומה, you may put small vessels inside a big one and dip them all together in the מקוה. For קודש, each vessel must be dipped on its own. Also, for תרומה, if one part of a vessel (outside, inside, or handle area) becomes impure, the other parts stay pure. For קודש, the whole vessel counts as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: They dip (in a מקוה) to purify
The outside (back) and the inside of a vessel
The place where a vessel is gripped

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying תרומה has no purity rules. Both need purity. קודש just has extra layers of strictness.

phrases.english: There is greater strictness with sacrificial food than with terumah,
for one may immerse vessels inside vessels for terumah,
but not for sacrificial food.
The back, the inside, and the gripping place [are separate] for terumah,
but not for sacrificial food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קודש, vessels may not be dipped inside other vessels, and the parts of a vessel are not treated separately. For תרומה, both of these leniencies are allowed.

steps.title: Carrying a מדרס, and the clothing of תרומה eaters
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. A person carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה but not קודש. Clothing of people who eat תרומה counts as a מדרס for קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone carrying a מדרס may carry תרומה, but not קודש. The clothes of people who eat תרומה are treated as a מדרס when it comes to קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing ways that קודש is stricter than תרומה. These two rules are about what you may carry, and about clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מדרס is something a זב has sat or leaned on, which makes it impure. You may carry it together with תרומה if you are careful, but never together with קודש. Also, clothes that are pure enough for people eating תרומה are still treated as fully impure (like a מדרס) for קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: An item made impure by a זב sitting, lying, or leaning on it
The clothes of those who eat תרומה

steps.whyThisMatters: These rules show that the purity level good enough for תרומה is not good enough for קודש. Even clothing that seems fine must be treated as impure near קודש.

phrases.english: One who carries a midras
phrases.notes: A מדרס is an item that a זב has sat or leaned on, which makes it impure.

phrases.english: may carry terumah,
but not sacrificial food.
The garments of those who eat terumah
are a midras for sacrificial food.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַמִּדְרָס, נוֹשֵׂא אֶת הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of ways קודש is stricter than תרומה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may carry a מדרס together with תרומה but not with קודש. Clothes of תרומה eaters count as a מדרס for קודש.

steps.title: Knots: untie before dipping for holy food, not for terumah
steps.stepSummary: For קודש, a knotted item must be untied, dried, dipped, and only then retied. For תרומה, one may tie it and then dip it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule for תרומה is not like the rule for קודש. With קודש, a person unties, dries, and dips, and only afterward ties again. With תרומה, he may tie and then dip.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new list of differences with a heading line: תרומה is not treated like קודש. Its first example is about an item with a knot that needs to be dipped in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קודש, the knot must be undone first so nothing can stop the water from reaching every part of the item. Then it is dried, dipped, and only retied afterward. For תרומה, the knot is not treated as a problem, so he can tie it and dip it as is.

keyTerms.meaning: The standard (rules) used for holy sacrificial food
He dips it in a מקוה

phrases.english: The rule of teruma is not like the rule of sacred food.
For with sacred food: one unties, dries, and immerses,
phrases.notes: He means an item tied with a knot that needs dipping in a מקוה.

phrases.english: and afterward ties it.
But with teruma: one ties, and afterward immerses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of stringencies of קודש over תרומה with a new heading and the knot rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קודש, a knot must be untied, the item dried and dipped, then retied. For תרומה, one may tie and then dip.

steps.title: New vessels made in purity still need dipping for holy food
steps.stepSummary: Vessels finished while kept pure still need טבילה before use with קודש, but not before use with תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vessels that were finished in purity need dipping for use with קודש, but not for use with תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another difference. A vessel made carefully in purity can be used right away for תרומה, but for קודש it must first be dipped in a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These vessels were never actually made impure. For תרומה, that is enough. For קודש, the משנה demands an extra dipping anyway, because people worry more about the purity of holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels whose making was finished in purity

phrases.english: Vessels that are completed in purity
require immersion for sacred food,
but not for teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּלִים הַנִּגְמָרִים בְּטָהֳרָה צְרִיכִין טְבִילָה לַקֹּדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of stringencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels made in purity need טבילה for קודש, not for תרומה.

steps.title: A vessel joins all the food inside it for holy food
steps.stepSummary: With קודש, all the separate pieces of food in one vessel count as one unit for impurity. With תרומה they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A vessel joins together whatever is inside it for קודש, but not for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another difference. If one piece of קודש in a vessel becomes impure, all the pieces in that vessel are treated as impure. With תרומה, each piece stays separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, separate pieces of food that are not touching do not pass impurity to each other. For קודש, being in the same vessel is enough to link them together as one. For תרומה, each piece is judged on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together, combines into one unit

phrases.english: The vessel combines what is inside it
for sacred food, but not for teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of stringencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קודש, a vessel unites all food inside it for impurity. For תרומה, it does not.

steps.title: Holy food is ruined even at the fourth level of impurity
steps.stepSummary: קודש becomes פסול even at the fourth level of impurity. תרומה only goes down to the third level.
steps.simpleTranslation: A fourth level in קודש is disqualified, and a third level in תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares how far impurity can spread. Impurity passes down step by step in levels, and קודש can be ruined at a lower level than תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impurity weakens with each step it is passed along. תרומה can be ruined by impurity only as far as the third level, so a fourth level does not affect it. קודש is so sensitive that even the fourth level disqualifies it.
steps.confusionAlert: פסול here does not mean it spreads impurity further. It means the food itself is ruined, but it does not make other things impure.

phrases.english: The fourth degree in sacred food is disqualified,
and the third degree in teruma.
phrases.notes: Read the word 'disqualified' into this line too. The משנה says it once and means it for both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of stringencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קודש is disqualified at the fourth level of impurity. תרומה is disqualified only down to the third.

steps.title: One impure hand makes the other impure for holy food
steps.stepSummary: For תרומה, if one hand is impure, the other stays pure. For קודש, he must dip both hands, because one hand makes the other impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: With תרומה, if one of his hands became impure, the other hand is pure. With קודש, he dips both, because one hand makes the other impure for קודש but not for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to hands. It gives the case, the ruling for each kind of food, and then the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תרומה, each hand is treated on its own, so only the impure hand needs fixing. For קודש, the impure hand is considered to pass its impurity to the other hand. So both hands must be dipped.

phrases.english: And with teruma, if one of his hands became impure,
its partner is pure.
But with sacred food, he immerses both of them,
because the hand makes its partner impure
for sacred food, but not for teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִתְרוּמָה אִם נִטְמֵאת אַחַת מִיָּדָיו חֲבֶירְתָּהּ טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of stringencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For קודש, one impure hand makes the other impure, so both need טבילה. For תרומה, the other hand stays pure.

steps.title: Dry food may be eaten with impure hands only for terumah
steps.stepSummary: One may eat dry foods with impure hands when the food is תרומה, but not when it is קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may eat dry foods with impure hands when they are תרומה, but not when they are קודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes this group with a rule about eating dry food while one's hands are impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dry food that never got wet cannot pick up impurity, so the impure hands should not matter. For תרומה, that is the rule. For קודש, חכמים are stricter and do not allow it even then.
steps.whatToRemember: Every item in this משנה follows one pattern: a strict rule for קודש and a lenient one for תרומה. The point is that holy sacrificial food gets extra purity protection.
steps.whyThisMatters: This last case shows how far the stringency goes. Even food that technically cannot become impure is protected when it is קודש.

phrases.english: One may eat dry foods
with impure hands in the case of teruma,
but not in the case of sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹכְלִין אוֹכָלִים נְגוּבִין בְּיָדַיִם מְסוֹאָבוֹת בִתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in this section of the list of stringencies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry foods may be eaten with impure hands for תרומה but not for קודש.
